To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Ser216 in MltB is essential for its catalytic activity and that this serine is involved in substrate orientation and stabilization in the −1 subsites.
the Ser216 residue in Pseudomonasaeruginosa membrane‐ bound lytic transglycoylase B (MLTB) plays a key role in the enzyme’s substrate‐assisted reaction mechanism.
Ser216 in P. aeruginosa MltB plays a role in substrate binding and in the enzyme's catalytic mechanism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the mechanism of action and the structural basis for substrate specificity of MltB.
the elucidation of the mechanism of action for membrane‐bound MltB, a member of the bacterial cell wall hydrolase superfamily.
the elucidation of the catalytic mechanism of lytic transglycolases, enzymes that cleave the β1,4 glycosidic bond between N‐acetylluramic acid (NAM) and N‐acylglucosamine residues in peptidoglucans.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Ser216 is a key residue in the catalytic mechanism of action of MltB, but not for substrate recognition.

substrate‐assisted mechanisms of lysozyme, endolysins and lytic transglycolases are not identical, but they are all based on the same concept, i.e. the N‐acetoxy group on the N‐acetic moiety of the N‐acetal group of MurNAc or GlcNAc is involved in the cleavage of the β‐( 1 → 4 ) glycosidic bond.
the mechanism of MltB involves the formation of a tetrahedral intermediate with substrate‐assisted protonation, followed by the release of the product and the regeneration of the enzyme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the catalytic mechanism of MltB involves substrate‐assisted hydrolysis of the glycosidic bond, and this is achieved by a combination of the catalytic triad Ser216–His217–Asp218, which provides the catalytic machinery, and the N‐acetoxy group of MurNAc, which acts as a nucleophilic catalyst.

the mechanism of action for the membrane‐bound MltB is similar to that of the cytoplasmic MltA. The latter enzyme, which has been studied in great detail, is believed to catalyze the reaction via a substrate‐assistance mechanism.

the catalytic mechanism for lytic transglycolysis involves substrate‐assisted general acid catalysis by Ser216 and a base catalyzed by His217, which acts as a general base to activate water for the nucleophilic attack on the glycosidic bond.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the substrate‐assisted reaction mechanism is conserved among lytic transglycolases, including those from Gram‐negative bacteria.
the catalytic role of Ser216 is not restricted to MltB but is likely shared by other membrane‐bound lysozymes.
Ser216 in MltB is a key residue for substrate‐assistant catalysis, and its replacement with alanine severely affects the enzyme's catalytic activity.
